extracted.intended_audience: USPTO management, auditors, oversight bodies, and users of USPTO financial statements (Congress, OMB, stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for USPTO financial reporting, program cost allocation, fiduciary handling, and internal control (including IT general controls) as used in the FY2016 Performance & Accountability Report and the independent audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding limitations under Leahy–Smith America Invents Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Leahy–Smith America Invents Act (35 U.S.C. §42(c)), all fees available to the Director under section 31 of the Trademark Act of 1946 are used only for the processing of trademark registrations and for other activities, services, and materials relating to trademarks, as well as to cover a proportionate share of the administrative costs of the USPTO. Pursuant to the Leahy–Smith America Invents Act (35 U.S.C. §42(c)), all fees available to the Director under sections 41, 42, and 376 of 35 U.S.C. are used only for the processing of patent applications and for other activities, services, and materials relating to patents, as well as to cover a proportionate share of the administrative costs of the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees collected under the cited statutory sections are restricted to use for the specific processing and related activities (patent or trademark) and to cover a proportionate share of USPTO administrative costs. This is a statutory funding limitation that constrains budgeting and expenditure classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program costs assignment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Program costs consist of both costs related directly to the individual business lines and overall support costs allocated to the business lines. All costs are assigned to specific programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total program or operating costs are reported by cost category and business line (e.g., patent, trademark, intellectual property protection). Costs are split into direct and allocated components and summed to produce total program costs for each responsibility segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program cost categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Total program or operating costs are reported by detailed cost categories such as Personnel Services and Benefits; Travel and Transportation; Rent, Communications, and Utilities; Printing and Reproduction; Contractual Services; Training; Maintenance and Repairs; Supplies and Materials; Equipment not Capitalized; Insurance Claims and Indemnities; Depreciation, Amortization, or Loss on Asset Dispositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial reporting must present direct and allocated amounts by these categories (dollars in thousands shown). These categories align to budget object classes and support the Schedule of Spending and Statement of Budgetary Resources reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation and reporting of allocated costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocated costs (examples shown: Automation, Resource Management) are reported separately and subtotaled as 'Allocated Costs' before combining with Direct Costs to form Total Program Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocated costs must be tracked and apportioned to business lines with subtotals presented to show how direct and allocated costs combine into total program costs by responsibility segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiduciary activities policy and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiduciary activities are the collection or receipt, and the management, protection, accounting, and disposition by the federal government of cash or other assets in which non-federal individuals or entities have an ownership interest that the federal government must uphold. Fiduciary cash and other assets are not assets of the federal government and accordingly are not recognized on the proprietary financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO is authorized (e.g., by the Patent Cooperation Treaty and the Madrid Protocol Implementation Act) to collect patent filing/search fees and trademark application fees on behalf of international IP offices. Fiduciary funds must be presented in a Schedule of Fiduciary Activity, showing contributions, disbursements to beneficiaries, changes in fiduciary net assets, and cash/equivalents, and are excluded from proprietary statement asset recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred maintenance and repairs (DM&R) definition and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferred maintenance and repairs are maintenance and repairs that were not performed when they should have been, that were scheduled and not performed, or that were delayed for a future period. Maintenance and repairs exclude activities aimed at expanding capacity or upgrading assets to serve different or significantly greater needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PP&E at the USPTO (furniture, IT equipment, office/telecom equipment, leasehold improvements, internal use software) must be maintained in acceptable operating condition. The USPTO conducts periodic user feedback, prioritizes projects, maintains warranties, and replaces equipment on a regular cycle to keep operations and maintenance costs stable; accordingly, DM&R do not arise for USPTO PP&E and no periodic assessment is performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit standards and audit opinion expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent audit was performed in accordance with U.S. generally accepted auditing standards, Government Auditing Standards, and OMB Bulletin 15-02, Audit Requirements for Federal Financial Statements. The auditor's responsibility is to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free from material misstatement and to express an opinion on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors evaluate accounting policies, significant estimates, and overall presentation; test compliance with certain laws/regulations as they relate to financial statements; and may provide an unmodified (clean) opinion if statements are fairly presented. Audit scope and limitations (e.g., not expressing opinion on internal control effectiveness) should be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of internal control deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: A deficiency in internal control exists when the design or operation of a control does not allow management or employees to prevent, or detect and correct, misstatements on a timely basis. A material weakness is a deficiency or combination of deficiencies with reasonable possibility that a material misstatement will not be prevented or detected. A significant deficiency is less severe than a material weakness but important enough to merit attention by those charged with governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors should describe any identified deficiencies and classify them (material weakness, significant deficiency). The report should disclose whether any material weaknesses were identified and provide details on significant deficiencies (Exhibit I in this audit).

rubrics_metrics.name: IT general controls objectives and referenced standards
rubrics_metrics.description: General controls include security management, logical and physical access, configuration management, segregation of duties, and contingency planning. The audit considered DOC and USPTO policies and Federal standards such as GAO's Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government, GAO's FISCAM, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4, and NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IT general controls should be designed to support management's ability to ensure transactions are complete, accurate, and valid. Audits of IT controls should be aligned to GAO and NIST guidance; sensitive IT control information may be omitted from public reports and provided in limited-distribution IT reports to management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access controls expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives of limiting access are to ensure users have only the access needed to perform duties; that access to sensitive resources (e.g., security software) is limited to few individuals; and that employees are restricted from performing incompatible functions beyond their responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key control areas include database and operating system password controls, access administration controls, and logical access controls. Deficiencies in these areas constitute IT general control weaknesses and should be remediated via corrective action plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configuration management expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives of configuration management are to ensure hardware, software and firmware programs, and program modifications are properly authorized, tested, and approved; that access to and distribution of programs is carefully controlled; and that integrity of the application controls is maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configuration and patch management are critical subcomponents; deficiencies (e.g., unauthorized changes, inadequate patching) are reportable as IT control weaknesses and require corrective actions. A separate limited-distribution IT report may provide specific findings and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation of net cost of operations to budget
rubrics_metrics.description: A reconciliation is provided to identify relationships and differences between budgetary and proprietary accounts. It breaks out resources used to finance activities (obligations incurred, spending authority from offsetting collections and recoveries, imputed financing), resources used to finance items not part of net cost of operations, and components of net cost that will/will not require resources in future periods (e.g., depreciation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reconciliation should present numeric subtotals (resources generated to finance activities, resources used for items not part of net cost, total components not requiring resources) and reconcile to Net Income from Operations. It clarifies timing and accounting differences between budgetary and proprietary reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Spending reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Schedule of Spending provides an overview of how and where the USPTO is obligating money: total resources available, amounts not agreed to be spent, amounts not available to be spent, total amounts agreed to be spent, how the money was spent (aligned to OMB budget object classes), and who received the money (federal vs non-federal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts in the Schedule of Spending should agree to Obligations Incurred on the Statement of Budgetary Resources and present personnel compensation and benefits and other object classes with totals for federal and non-federal recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custodial collections treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Custodial collections represent miscellaneous general fund receipts (e.g., non-electronic patent filing fees, foreign exchange gains, employee debt finance charges). Custodial collection activities are considered immaterial and incidental to the mission of the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Custodial activity should be presented showing revenue activity, sources of collections, accrual adjustments, disposition of collections (transferred to Treasury), and any increase/decrease in amounts yet to be transferred. If immaterial/incidental, the net custodial activity may be zero after transfer.
